articles.title: Past interpersonal trauma can shape current relationship conflict tactics
articles.summary: How people manage disagreements with romantic partners relies heavily on their attachment orientation. A recent study reveals that individuals with insecure attachments are less likely to compromise and more prone to confrontational or submissive behaviors during relationship disputes.

articles.title: Two new compounds could reveal hidden drivers of Alzheimer’s disease
articles.summary: Vanderbilt researchers created the first selective compound designed to inhibit TAOK-1, a poorly understood protein connected to Alzheimer’s disease. They also discovered a second compound that activates the entire TAOK protein family, offering scientists an unexpected new research tool. Together, the compounds could reveal hidden disease mechanisms and point toward new treatment strategies.

articles.title: Scientists may have found aging’s hidden trigger for brain disease
articles.summary: Scientists have identified a molecular switch that may help explain why aging makes the brain more vulnerable to diseases such as ALS and Huntington’s. In worms, the protein EPS8 builds up with age and triggers signaling that encourages toxic proteins to clump together, damaging neurons and shortening lifespan. Reducing EPS8 activity prevented these harmful aggregates and preserved nerve function.

articles.title: Friends tend to be somewhat closer if their demographic characteristics are similar
articles.summary: Do birds of a feather really flock together? A new study suggests that sharing demographic traits, such as age and gender, is linked to higher emotional closeness in friendships, especially for women and outgoing individuals.

articles.title: Can AI Evaluate AI Scientists? A Benchmarking Study of Autonomous Research Generation Systems Using Automated Multi-Model Review
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.28631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI Scientist systems capable of autonomous research have the potential to significantly accelerate scientific discovery. However, evaluating and comparing the quality of AI-generated papers remains an open challenge. We propose and implement a rigorous benchmarking protocol using an automated peer-review system that harnesses frontier large language models to assess scientific papers across four core dimensions: originality, scientific rigor, clarity, and significance. We evaluate four leading AI Scientist frameworks: \textit{Sakana AI (v1 & v2)}

articles.title: ThinkReset: Learnable Intermediate Interface Construction for Bounded-Context Long-Horizon Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.28642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long chain-of-thought reasoning improves performance on complex problems, but it also introduces redundancy accumulation, context overflow, and error anchoring. We argue that under bounded context windows, the core bottleneck is not trajectory compression or test-time control, but the absence of a reusable intermediate interface that can replace discarded history and support continued solving. We further identify a key failure mode of outcome-reward-driven long-chain reinforcement learning: when the model has not solved the task before the window

articles.title: Men with atypical testosterone levels face a higher risk of depression
articles.summary: Men whose testosterone levels fall unusually high or low for their age group face an increased risk of developing depression. A large study suggests that midlife is a particularly vulnerable period for these hormone-related mental health risks.

articles.title: Topology-Aware Data Movement for Disaggregated GPU Inference
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.28633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disaggregated LLM inference creates a datacenter networking problem that no existing system solves correctly. When prefill and decode run on separate GPU pools, the KV cache must be transferred between them. For a 70B model this is 2.6 GB per request, exceeding 100 GB/s aggregate at production scale. Yet DistServe, Splitwise, and Mooncake all use uniform RDMA, ignoring that bandwidth between two GPUs varies by 72x depending on their physical relationship: 900 GB/s via NVLink within a domain, 50 GB/s via InfiniBand across nodes, 12.5 GB/s via TCP

articles.title: But What Behavior?
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.28898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What is a natural behavior? I argue that the study of natural behaviors is often the study of the spontaneous behaviors of animals placed in quantifiably different environments. For behavioral generalists such as rodents, humans, and many other species, there may be no such definable construct as a native habitat or natural behavior, due to their successful abilities and needs to rapidly adapt to a wide range of different ecosystems. articles.title: Parental high-fat diets leave lasting marks on offspring brain development
articles.summary: A parent's diet before and during pregnancy leaves lasting physical marks on offspring brains. A new mouse study shows that parental high-fat diets alter brain structure into adulthood, even if the offspring transition to healthy eating.

articles.title: Eye tracking reveals the hidden power of painted hands
articles.summary: A new eye-tracking experiment reveals that the pointing gestures painted into classic artworks secretly act as guides for human vision. Even though viewers barely look at the painted hands, these small details completely reshape how we understand the artwork.
